topic: light-colour: changing the colour and intensity of a zone's lights at runtime
method: ilspycmd 11.0.0.9375 (%TEMP%\codex-ilspy) against the QA profile's interop assemblies (%APPDATA%\r2modmanPlus-local\GTFO\profiles\Forge-MapEditor-QA\BepInEx\interop\Modules-ASM.dll, sha256 E499B9C0EB1FA4F1C4194B13163CE1932355AD20C04C424FE4661F8EEF736D63). Metadata only: no game was started, no hook was installed and no level was built. The wrapper bodies are il2cpp_runtime_invoke stubs, so no row here claims what a call does in a running level — only that the member exists, its signature and that it is a runtime-invoke wrapper.

findings.member: public unsafe Color m_color { get; set; }
findings.wrapper: Il2CppInterop field accessor over NativeFieldInfoPtr_m_color; the getter reads the field of the live light object.
findings.why: It is the light's own current colour, which is the value a transition has to start from when a second request arrives while one is still running.

findings.member: public unsafe LG_Light.LightCategory m_category { get; set; }
findings.why: The category is what a request that names one filters on, and it is the unit the block's own settings are written per (GameData.LightCategorySetting.Category).

The read a transition needs to turn a brightness multiplier into an absolute intensity; it is the game's own getter rather than the m_intensity field, so a light kind that overrides it answers its real intensity.

findings.wrapper: il2cpp_runtime_invoke stub; Public Virtual New, so a concrete light kind's override is what runs.
findings.why: One step of a colour transition. There is no gradient entry on a light, so the frames are this package's (LightColorFade).
One step of an intensity transition, and the write a request that names only a colour leaves alone.

findings.member: public unsafe void SetEnabled(bool enabled) and public unsafe void SetEnabled(bool enabled, string reason)
findings.why: Recorded because it exists, but this row does not call it: on/off stays the game's own light events (`forge.action.presentation.lighting`) so the level's own state replicator keeps owning it.

findings.wrapper: Il2CppInterop field accessor; the entry list of the zone, not a copy.
findings.why: The one place a level records which lights a zone holds, so it is the recipient list every request resolves. Already registered with its wrapper type in evidence/map1-2026-09-12/native-api.json (LG_Zone, m_lightsInZone, lines 405-417); the same file records m_lightSettings and m_lightsSubSeed as readable and writable, which this row deliberately does not write — the block is the level's build-time input and is commonly shared between zones.

findings.member: public unsafe List<LightCategorySetting> LightCategorySettings { get; set; }
findings.wrapper: il2cpp_runtime_invoke stubs over the backing field (get token 100679544, set token 100679543).
findings.why: The block's whole content: one entry per light category. Recorded so the website-side block the compiler generates (site/map-zone-light.ts, bound to Zones[i].LightSettings) is the same shape the game reads.

findings.member: public unsafe bool On; public unsafe LG_Light.LightCategory Category; public unsafe float Chance; public unsafe float ChanceBroken; public unsafe Color Color; public unsafe float IntensityMul; public unsafe float Weight
findings.wrapper: Il2CppInterop field accessors over the backing fields.
findings.why: The fields a block entry actually carries. The generated block writes On, Category, Chance, ChanceBroken, Color, IntensityMul and Weight and nothing else; the vanilla table (99 blocks in the website preview data) uses categories 0-6 with Weight 1 and Chance 0/0.5/1, which is the vocabulary the generator follows.

derived.fact: the lights one light-colour request writes
derived.derivation: EnvironmentZoneTable.At(address) | EnvironmentZoneTable.Standing() -> LG_Zone.m_lightsInZone -> entries whose m_category matches the request (or every entry) -> ChangeColor/ChangeIntensity through LightColorFade
derived.refusal: A zone the level does not have, a zone with no light object and a zone with no light of the requested category are each refused by name (light-color-no-lights) before the first write; a request that names neither a colour nor a brightness is refused rather than served as a transition to what the lights already are (light-color-required).

derived.fact: the frames a transition runs on
derived.derivation: the session's one kernel clock (MapClock, observing RuntimeLifecycleKind.TickAdvanced through the map-object module's registration and taken only while a transition is in flight) -> Plugin.Session.WorldEpoch -> LightColorFades.Tick(worldEpoch, Time.deltaTime)
derived.refusal: A frame with no session clears the table, and a tick whose world is not the table's drops it instead of writing at light objects the level teardown already took; a light that throws on a write is dropped from its own transition and leaves the others of the same frame running.

notVerifiedInGame: Whether ChangeColor/ChangeIntensity survive the level's own passes over the same lights: EMP, door and alarm logic, distance culling, and the light settings job that runs when a zone is (re)built. Nothing static says who runs last.

Whether a colour written this way is visible on any machine but the one that ran the request. EnvironmentStateManager's light entries are the two on/off flips, and the light objects themselves are local to a process, so the row claims the process it runs in and says so; a replicated version needs a game-side answer that static evidence cannot give.

The order and meaning of LG_Light.LightCategory's values. The enum exists (EnumUtil.GetValueLength<LG_Light.LightCategory> in dump.cs:344139) and the vanilla table only ever uses 0-6, which is the vocabulary this row accepts by name; the enum's declaration itself was not read as IL.

What Color.a means for a light. The vanilla table carries 0, 1 and intermediate values, so a block the compiler generates copies the alpha of the same category out of the block the zone already referenced rather than choosing one.
Whether ChangeIntensity on a light that is off changes what the player sees when it is switched back on.

evidenceSources.decompiled: Modules-ASM.dll via ilspycmd: LevelGeneration.LG_Light (m_color, m_category, GetIntensity, ChangeColor, ChangeIntensity, SetEnabled), GameData.LightSettingsDataBlock, GameData.LightCategorySetting
